THEY EXPECTED FLAT SEAFLOOR — INSTEAD, THEY FOUND THIS 
At 3.4 miles beneath the Pacific Ocean, scientists expected to find a mostly flat abyssal plain.

But the ROV revealed something completely different.

Large volcanic boulders, pillow lavas and rugged terrain covered the seafloor—more like a hidden underwater mountain landscape than a flat plain.

And growing among the rocks was a 5.3-foot bamboo whip coral that may represent a depth record for its type.

🌊 How many hidden landscapes are still waiting beneath the ocean?
